idiom_name: const SecurityContext& parameter through the call chain
implementation_notes: The default C++ realization keeps the security context an ordinary object passed as a const reference to every component that needs it, so the type system records the dependency instead of a comment. Lifetimes stay deterministic (the request owns the context on the stack), a guard cannot read someone else's identity, and testing is a matter of constructing a context. Reach for the holder form only where a callback signature cannot be extended; on C++11 and later that is the thread_local plus RAII variant.
pitfalls: Do not store the context in a long-lived object: it belongs to one request, so keep a reference only for the dynamic extent of that request.
Passing the context by value copies the attributes on every call; pass by reference and keep the context immutable.
A default-constructed context must never mean "privileged": give the type no permissive default state.

variants.name: thread_local holder with an RAII scoped binder (C++11)
variants.idiom_name: thread_local current pointer plus a scoped binder object
variants.implementation_notes: C++11 thread storage duration (thread_local, documented under storage class specifiers on cppreference) makes an ambient holder possible, and RAII makes it safe: a ScopedContext object exchanges the current thread-local pointer in its constructor and restores the previous value in its destructor, so early returns and exceptions unbind correctly where manual set/reset code would not. Use it when a guard cannot receive the context as a parameter; prefer the explicit reference everywhere else, because the binding is invisible and does not follow work onto another thread or into a coroutine.
pitfalls: Restoring the previous binding matters under nesting: a nested handler that binds its own context must not erase its caller's on exit.
Executors and C++20 coroutines do not inherit thread_local values, so a continuation resumed elsewhere sees a different or null context - pass the context into the task explicitly.
A thread_local holder is per-thread state on pooled threads; the scoped binder is what guarantees the next request cannot see the previous principal, so never bind without it.
